data.name: Andriette
data.gender_notes: Andriette is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name Andreas, meaning man, Andriette is a female variation of the name. It signifies a strong, brave woman, as the root name Andreas is derived from the Greek word andros, meaning man. The name Andriette carries the meaning “Andr- woman, ette- small” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Andriette usually hope their child will grow to embody andr- woman, ette- small and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Andriette total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

in_greek.name: Ανδριέτ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ανδριέτ είναι ελληνικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη Ανδριάς, η οποία σημαίνει άνδρας. Η λέξη Ανδριάς είναι σύνθετη από το ανδρός και η αλήθεια. Το όνομα Ανδριέτ έχει ιστορία στην Καινή Διαθήκη, όπου το όνομα Ανδρέας ήταν δημοφιλές στην αρχαία Ελλάδα. Το όνομα Ανδριέτ είναι επίσης γνωστό ως μια επώνυμη μορφή από την ελληνική λέξη Ανδριάς, η οποία σημαίνει άνδρας.

in_latin.name: Andriette
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Andriette est nomen femininum quod significat masculinum. Auctoritas nominis Andriette in historia Ecclesiae Christi est notissima, cum nomen Andreas fuerit in usu antiquo in Ecclesia Christi. Andriette est nomen femininum quod significat masculinum, et est forma nominis Andriás.

In the Bible, the name Andreas is mentioned in the New Testament as one of Jesus' twelve apostles. Andriette is a modern feminine form of the name Andreas, which is associated with the qualities of strength and courage. In Christian tradition, the name Andriette is given to children born to parents who value these qualities and want their child to embody them.
